diagnostic_facts.causal_interpretation_limit: The single-case diagnostic identifies the numerical mechanism of the observed failure but cannot estimate a cross-case output-error distribution or calibrate a new output tolerance.

rationale: The frozen theoretical identity is invariance of softmax to a common additive logit shift, so attention is the construct-aligned functional quantity.
The observed attention discrepancy is 1.3969838619232178e-09, only 0.0013969838619232178 of the already frozen 1e-6 attention threshold.
Retaining the existing 1e-6 attention threshold avoids tuning a new threshold from the failed case.
A per-case attention gate across all future authorized Round A-I cases remains fail-closed for an incorrect intervention or materially nonuniform bias.
Raw logits must differ by the intended common shift and therefore must not be compared directly for equality.
Row-centering is useful for locating nonconstant finite-precision residue, but the centering operation introduces its own magnitude-dependent FP32 rounding.
The one-case value 3.5762786865234375e-07 is descriptive evidence, not an independently justified acceptance threshold.
Attention directly tests the functional softmax invariance and is already available in the current formal instrumentation.
Only one case has stage-wise scalar evidence, so neither a percentile nor a worst-case output tolerance can be estimated reliably.
Output error depends on downstream decoder sensitivity as well as normalization scale; millimetre conversion alone is not a sufficient conditioning model.
Choosing a new output threshold after observing the failing value would be post-hoc threshold tuning.
Output-level equality is not the mathematical claim made by the case-mean softmax negative control.
